description: The three stages run from left to right. The table lists each stage's goal, material, and suggested method. Below stages 2 and 3, an upward arrow connects each method box to its stage. Stage 1 has no separate method box.

frames.explanation: A one-way arrow leads from stage 1 to stage 2. Two arrows pointing in opposite directions connect stages 2 and 3. After reaching stage 3, you can return to stage 2 for more problems, so practice and organizing your knowledge reinforce each other.
frames.title: A learning path for algorithms

summary: Move from the basics to practice problems and a connected understanding of the subject. Periodic review and summarizing what you learn help deepen that understanding.

tables.caption: Three stages of learning and their methods
rows: Review periodically: revisit the same problem at intervals to retain it and deepen your understanding.
Algorithm articles, problem-solving frameworks, and algorithms textbooks
Summarize what you learn: organize the material and identify patterns to build a coherent understanding.
